title: Beating impulse spending — the 24-hour rule and friction
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Impulse spending is driven by emotion, discounts and convenience — one-tap UPI, food delivery and flash sales make it easy. Practical fixes: use a 24-hour rule for any non-essential purchase above a small limit (₹1,000 is common); remove saved cards and unsubscribe from sale emails; give yourself a fixed monthly 'fun money' amount so guilt-free spending has a boundary; split your accounts so savings are not one tap away; convert prices into work hours (price divided by your hourly income) to feel their real cost; and review your last 30 days of spending to find the two or three leaks that matter most. Cutting a small, recurring leak such as unused subscriptions or daily delivery often saves more than a big one-time sacrifice.
summary_hinglish: Impulse spending emotion, discount aur one-tap UPI se hoti hai. 24-ghante ka rule lagao (₹1,000 se upar ki non-essential cheez), saved cards hatao, mahine ka fixed 'fun money' rakho, savings alag account mein rakho, aur price ko work-hours mein convert karke dekho. Chhote recurring leaks (subscriptions, delivery) aksar sabse zyada bachate hain.
summary_hi: आवेग में खर्च भावना, छूट और वन-टैप UPI से होता है। गैर-ज़रूरी खरीद पर 24 घंटे का नियम रखें, सेव्ड कार्ड हटाएं, महीने का तय 'फन मनी' रखें, बचत अलग खाते में रखें और कीमत को कार्य-घंटों में बदलकर देखें। छोटे आवर्ती रिसाव (सब्सक्रिप्शन, डिलीवरी) अक्सर सबसे ज़्यादा बचाते हैं।
